sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: See how a real sorority inspired Delta Nu's pink look.

factBeats.text: Costume designer Sophie de Rakoff and Reese Witherspoon visited a sorority house for research while prepping for the film.
During their visit, they observed that everyone at the real sorority was wearing pink.
This observation became a "throughline for the movie" and a key part of the overall aesthetic.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: See where Elle Woods really went to "Harvard"?

factBeats.text: While the story places Elle Woods at Harvard, the university itself didn't allow filming on its campus.
Instead, the production filmed the "Harvard" campus scenes at various institutes across California.
This particular scene, where Elle arrives and picks up her class schedule, was shot on the patio of Kerckhoff Hall at UCLA.
Another "Harvard" square seen in the film was the rector's house of All Saints Church in Pasadena.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: Discover the inspiration behind Elle's iconic pink style.
sceneFacts.factHeader: Elle's colorful laptop reflects her unique style.

factBeats.text: Costume designer Sophie de Rakoff established Elle's signature pink aesthetic after observing sorority life during research for the film.
This "broad and varied palette" was largely due to Elle's "ever-changing wardrobe" throughout the film.
The author of the original novel, Amanda Brown, also embraced a similar personal style, writing her manuscript on pink paper with a pink furry pen.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: How did Elle's signature pink style come to be?

factBeats.text: Costume designer Sophie de Rakoff and Reese Witherspoon conducted research at a sorority house.
During their visit, they observed that everyone in the sorority house was wearing pink.
This observation established pink as a key aesthetic for Elle Woods' personality and identity in the movie.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: Discover how the trial changed from the book.
sceneFacts.factHeader: The murder trial wasn't in the original script

factBeats.text: The film is based on a 2001 novel by Amanda Brown, which was inspired by her own life experiences at Stanford Law School.
Screenwriters Karen McCullah and Kirsten Smith were brought on to adapt the book for the screen.
In the original manuscript, the central legal case was not a murder trial, and Elle ended up with a professor.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: What's the story behind Elle's iconic pink suit?
sceneFacts.factHeader: Elle's pink suit was a statement.

factBeats.text: When Elle Woods entered the courtroom in head-to-toe pink, she was upholding a cinematic tradition of using the color to intersect femininity and power.
Her outfit included a pink dress with a satin sash, cuffs, and lapels, paired with pink sandals, a pink bag, pink lips, and pink nails.
The design subtly referenced traditional male suiting with the shape of the cuffs and lapels, and even included sparkly cufflinks.
Costume designer Sophie de Rakoff stated that Elle "needed to be her most true self at this moment."
This entire outfit was a statement of Elle's confidence, self-knowledge, and refusal to let others diminish her.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: Spot the real-world location of Elle's graduation.
sceneFacts.factHeader: Elle's Harvard graduation was filmed across the pond.

factBeats.text: The final graduation ceremony was added to the film after test audiences were unsatisfied with earlier endings.
Test audiences didn't want the story to end with Elle getting a boyfriend, which was an earlier version of the finale.
By the time the graduation ending was decided, Reese Witherspoon was already in London filming another movie.
The "rousing finale" of Elle's graduation speech was filmed at Dulwich College in London.
